class.name: PBFParticleFluid3D
class.brief_description: Experimental native CPU particle fluid with position-based density constraints.
class.description: Simulates up to 2048 particles using Position Based Fluids (PBF): a compactly supported SPH kernel, iterative density constraints, deterministic sorted-cell neighbor lookup, artificial pressure and optional XSPH velocity smoothing. Unlike static fluid-plane buoyancy, particles move independently and can form a deforming free surface. Particle positions, velocities, box bounds, gravity and impulses are all in this node's [b]local coordinate system[/b]. The node does not create a visible mesh: render particles yourself with [MultiMeshInstance3D], a custom shader or a fluid surface renderer. See the Cgame Physics Lab sample for GPU-instanced sphere visualization. [b]Experimental:[/b] This is a bounded CPU demonstration of PBF, not a fully incompressible Navier-Stokes solver. The density constraint is one-sided (it prevents compression rather than forcing dilute free surfaces to expand). It does not implement viscosity between fluid and rigid bodies, surface reconstruction, GPU compute, solid boundary pressure or thermal/multiphase effects. A new optional vorticity confinement post-process restores small-scale vortices lost during PBF/XSPH and is disabled by default; it is a visual turbulence model, not a fully energy-conserving Navier-Stokes solver. Simple equal-and-opposite rigid-body contact impulses can be explicitly enabled through [member two_way_rigid_coupling]; this is not a continuum fluid-solid coupling solver. [b]Note:[/b] By default [member simulation_enabled], [member collide_with_bodies] and [member two_way_rigid_coupling] are [code]false[/code], so the class does no per-frame work. For manual stepping, use [method step] while simulation is disabled. The internal simulation tick runs in the regular physics frame. Parameters are intentionally capped to protect memory, runtime cost and numerical stability.

method.name: add_velocity_pulse
method.description: Adds a bounded, smooth radial impulse to particle velocities. Returns the number of affected particles. This is a velocity change, not a conserved Newton-second impulse, so it is intended for scripted stirring or splashes.

method.name: clear_particles
method.description: Clears the fluid's particle state and reusable neighbor-grid storage.

method.name: create_block
method.description: Creates a regularly spaced local-coordinate cuboid of liquid particles with zero initial velocities. The result is clamped to [member box_min] and [member box_max]. Returns [code]false[/code] without changing the previous particle state on invalid arguments or when the total count exceeds 2048.

method.name: get_average_density
method.description: Returns the mean SPH density measured in the latest PBF constraint pass. Zero before the first successful simulation step.

method.name: get_average_vorticity
method.description: Returns the mean magnitude of the SPH-estimated velocity curl, in inverse seconds, from the most recent enabled vorticity post-process. Returns zero if [member vorticity_confinement] is disabled or the particle set is cleared.

method.name: get_last_rigid_impulses
method.description: Returns the number of paired impulses transferred to rigid bodies in the most recent PBF substep. Zero when two-way coupling is disabled or no moving body is struck.

method.name: get_last_neighbor_evaluations
method.description: Returns the bounded number of neighbor interactions in the most recent substep. Useful for performance profiling; a particle can visit at most 128 neighbors during each solver iteration.

method.name: get_last_vorticity_neighbor_evaluations
method.description: Returns the number of neighborhood visits across all three vorticity passes (final density, curl and curl-magnitude gradient) in the most recent substep. The process is disabled at strength zero and bounded by three times the particle count times 128.

method.name: get_particle_count
method.description: Returns the number of live fluid particles (maximum 2048).

method.name: get_particle_positions
method.description: Returns a copy of the local-coordinate particle positions. Intended for rendering or inspection; avoid calling repeatedly for large batches.

method.name: get_particle_velocities
method.description: Returns a copy of the local-coordinate particle velocities.

method.name: set_particle_positions
method.description: Replaces all particles with these local positions and zero velocities, allocating reusable simulation buffers once. Rejects more than 2048 particles, nonfinite values, or out-of-range coordinates without mutating the current fluid state.

method.name: step
method.description: Advances the native fluid solver manually for [param delta] seconds. The step subdivides into at most eight segments of at most 1/60 second each. Returns [code]false[/code] for invalid or too-large timesteps. Do not also call this method while [member simulation_enabled] is enabled unless intentionally advancing the fluid twice.

Enables swept point-to-body ray collision for particles. By default this is one-way, with no reaction impulse on the solid. Enable [member two_way_rigid_coupling] to activate momentum exchange at dynamic rigid contacts.
Physics layers queried by the optional body collision sweep.
Fluid acceleration in the node's local space, in metres per second squared.

Maximum magnitude of an individual paired collision impulse, in N·s. Both the liquid particle and the dynamic rigid body use the same cap to preserve pairwise action and reaction. Extreme impacts may remain partially unresolved.
Particle mass for the SPH kernel and PBF density constraints.
Offset from tank walls and rigid-body hit points. This does not create individual sphere collision objects.
Target density for the unilateral PBF compression constraint.
SPH smoothing radius, also used as the width of each spatial grid cell.
Number of PBF density projection iterations per substep, clamped to 1–12.

Enables equal-and-opposite collision impulses between fluid particles and dynamic [RigidBody3D] surfaces. Uses contact speed, rigid mass, angular velocity and world-space inverse inertia for the normal effective mass. Requires [member collide_with_bodies]. Static and kinematic bodies retain one-way contacts. This does not model continuous pressure or buoyancy on immersed solids.

Controls opt-in vorticity confinement, which injects a bounded velocity change perpendicular to the SPH curl and to the gradient of its magnitude. Strength 0 disables all three extra neighbor passes. Positive values (up to 5 m/s) restore rotating flow lost during density projection and XSPH smoothing, but can inject kinetic energy and should not be confused with physical viscosity.

Upper limit in m/s on the additional particle velocity per simulation substep from vorticity confinement. Protects against extreme density gradients and large local velocity curls, at the cost of modifying the unconstrained vorticity force.
Blends neighboring particle velocities using an XSPH-style smoothing filter.
